entries.rationale: Switching the endocrine backbone from AI to fulvestrant is a downstream clinical decision triggered by suspected progression, ESR1 emergence, or AI intolerance; it is caused by treatment history but is not on the original-treatment->24m-PFS path (it is a response TO impending failure). Descendant; analyses that adjust for it would condition on a post-baseline event downstream of treatment. The descendant-vs-collider discriminator is whether the trigger is an INDEPENDENT prognostic parent of 24m-PFS or reduces to the patient's own T-driven trajectory, and the literature settles it toward T-driven: ESR1 mutations are essentially absent in treatment-naive disease and their frequency rises with cumulative endocrine exposure (Jeselsohn 2015 Nat Rev Clin Oncol; Bhave 2024 Breast Cancer Res Treat: ~8% first-line to ~59% third-line), i.e. T (aromatase inhibition) -> ESR1 emergence is acquired, treatment-driven resistance, exactly the monitor-rising-bESR1-then-switch scenario of PADA-1 (Bidard 2022 Lancet Oncol). The second arrow into the switch is therefore itself downstream of T (not an exogenous U->Y parent), satisfying the descendant carve-out. Caveat: 'AI intolerance' is cleanly T-driven and ESR1 emergence is the literature-backed leg; 'suspected progression' carries some treatment-independent disease biology, but the dominant, citable mechanism is T-driven, so descendant holds.

entries.rationale: Early-adopter physician status is a Brookhart-family short-term-IV variant: oncologists who initiated ribociclib within the first year post-FDA approval (2017-03-13) have a durable higher within-physician ribociclib preference (Z->T present; analogous to Brookhart 2006's within-physician prescription persistence). Exclusion-restriction (no Z->Y bypass): early-adopter status at the physician level does NOT affect the patient's tumor biology, ECOG, staging, or NCCN-standardized supportive-care infrastructure for CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib was FDA-approved in 2015, so early-adopter oncologists already had CDK4/6-class infrastructure in place — early ribociclib adoption is brand-specific, not class-specific). The plausible direct path 'early adopter -> better outcomes via general practice innovativeness' is addressable through case-mix balance audit (Rassen 2009) restricted to oncologists prescribing any CDK4/6 in the pre-2017 window. No common cause: physician adoption timing is exogenous to the index patient (the index patient was diagnosed after the adoption window). Brookhart 2010 catalogs adoption-timing instruments as a valid PPP variant.

entries.rationale: Brookhart 2006 introduced the most-recent-prior-prescription-by-same-physician as an IV. Z->T present: the previous CDK4/6 brand the oncologist prescribed strongly predicts what they will prescribe next (within-physician brand stickiness is documented in CDK4/6 PPP literature). Direct-path exclusion (no Z->Y bypass): the PRIOR patient's drug choice CANNOT affect THIS patient's tumor biology, ECOG, staging, monitoring intensity, or supportive-care infrastructure — those are all set by the index patient's own clinical context and by within-class CDK4/6 NCCN pathways that are identical across the three brands. The instrument operates on the brand-selection node only, not on care-quality nodes. No common cause: the oncologist's prior choice is exogenous to the index patient's prognostic factors (the index patient was not enrolled at the time of the prior prescription, and physician case mix is balanced across PPP strata per Rassen 2009). Canonical Brookhart PPP-IV.

entries.rationale: Physician prescribing preference (PPP) is the canonical pharmacoepi instrumental variable: variation in the treating oncologist's prior CDK4/6 brand mix predicts ribociclib exposure (relevance), is plausibly unrelated to the index patient's individual prognostic factors (exclusion), and there is no plausible direct effect of the oncologist's past prescribing on this patient's PFS except through treatment (independence). Brookhart 2006/2010 formalize the PPP-IV design; Rassen-Brookhart 2009 audit shows 25 PPP formulations strongly reduce covariate imbalance.

entries.rationale: Calendar-time discontinuity / policy-discontinuity IV per Brookhart 2010 (which explicitly catalogs calendar-time/policy-discontinuity as a valid IV family for comparative pharmacoepi research) and Hernan-Robins 2016 target-trial-emulation framework. Z->T present: the MONALEESA-3 first-line OS publication (Neven 2023) plus the accompanying NCCN preference shift caused a measurable step-change in ribociclib initiation. Exclusion-restriction (no Z->Y bypass): the calendar-window flag itself does NOT touch the patient's tumor biology, baseline staging, or supportive-care availability — those are determined by the patient's individual context at the moment of diagnosis, independent of which side of the discontinuity they fall on. Direct-path 'calendar -> general oncology care advances -> PFS' is closed by restricting to a NARROW 6-month window straddling the discontinuity (2022-10-18 +/- 6 months), within which secular trends in HR+/HER2- supportive care are negligible — this is the canonical ITS-with-narrow-bandwidth restriction (Brookhart 2010 sec. 4.3). No common cause: the publication date is exogenous to any individual patient's prognosis. Limitation acknowledged: requires explicit confounding-by-time-trend check (e.g., negative-control outcome that should NOT respond to the policy change, such as bone-metastasis rate at diagnosis).

entries.rationale: Regulatory natural-experiment / policy-discontinuity IV per Brookhart 2010 (which explicitly catalogs FDA-label-expansion timing as a valid IV family) plus Hernan-Robins 2016 target-trial-emulation framework. Z->T present: pre-vs-post FDA expansion (2018-07-12) sharply shifted access to ribociclib for premenopausal women — Z->T is by construction deterministic for the off side (pre-approval premenopausal women could not obtain on-label ribociclib). Exclusion-restriction (no Z->Y bypass): the calendar-discontinuity flag does NOT affect within-subgroup tumor biology, ovarian-suppression standard-of-care availability, or NCCN-pathway monitoring — those are time-invariant over the narrow window. Direct-path 'post-approval -> general advances in premenopausal MBC care -> PFS' is closed by restricting to a NARROW 12-month window straddling the discontinuity (2018-01-12 through 2019-01-12), within which secular trends in premenopausal HR+ care (notably ovarian suppression protocols, AI use) are negligible. No common cause: the FDA approval date is exogenous to any individual premenopausal patient's prognosis. Limitation: requires negative-control outcome audit (e.g., bone-density assessment rate) per Brookhart 2010 IV-validation checklist.

entries.rationale: Practice-level CDK4/6 brand share is a higher-aggregation cousin of the Brookhart PPP-IV (Z->T present via formulary defaults and detailing exposure). Exclusion-restriction defense for direct-care-path concerns: among the three FDA-approved CDK4/6 inhibitors, all three (palbociclib, ribociclib, abemaciclib) are dispensed by the SAME practice infrastructure, monitored on the SAME schedule per NCCN, and supported by the SAME oral-oncology adherence programs — so brand-share variation across practices does NOT correlate with overall oncology-care quality, monitoring intensity, or supportive-care infrastructure (which would otherwise affect PFS independent of brand). The direct path 'practice -> care quality -> PFS' is closed by holding the CDK4/6-class care pathway constant; the only remaining practice-level path to PFS is through brand-specific efficacy. Rassen-Brookhart 2009 demonstrate aggregate provider-preference formulations reduce imbalance across 25 variants, and Brookhart 2006 establishes that case-mix balance across PPP strata supports independence from unmeasured outcome causes. Audit per Brookhart 2010: stratify PPP by practice-type (community vs academic) and check covariate balance.

entries.rationale: Within-class switching pattern is a Brookhart-family PPP-IV variant capturing the prescriber's revealed preference for ribociclib given experience with palbociclib. Z->T present: high-switch-count oncologists are more likely to initiate ribociclib for any new patient (revealed brand preference). Exclusion-restriction (no Z->Y bypass): the count of OTHER patients' prior switches is exogenous to THIS patient's tumor biology, ECOG, staging, or care quality — switch decisions were made for distinct patients with their own clinical contexts. The prescriber's general care-quality is held constant across switch-count strata (a high-switch oncologist and a low-switch oncologist deliver the same NCCN-pathway monitoring for any given patient). No common cause: switch counts in OTHER patients are by construction not caused by the index patient's prognosis. Independence is supported by case-mix balance audit across switch-count tertiles (Rassen 2009). Brookhart 2006 formalizes within-physician prescription patterns; brand-switching is one of the 25 PPP variants Rassen-Brookhart audit.

Conditioning on it (e.g., restricting analysis to 180d-survivors) opens the back-door path T -> survival <- U -> Y, biasing the causal effect on UAS7 reduction. Must NOT be adjusted; instead handle via censoring weights or alternative outcome scale.

entries.rationale: On-treatment-at-180d (treatment persistence) is the canonical post-randomization collider per Hernan-Hernandez-Diaz-Robins 2004 (PMID 15308962) selection-bias framework, paralleling the alive-at-180d structure. Must NOT be adjusted in primary analyses; handle via intention-to-treat or inverse-probability-of-censoring weights.

entries.rationale: DLQI (Dermatology Life Quality Index) is a generic dermatology quality-of-life PRO instrument, NOT the CSU-primary disease-activity scale; the CSU-primary scales are UAS7 (signs/symptoms diary, used as the REMIX-1/2 primary endpoint per Metz 2025 NEJM) and UCT (4-item disease-control test per Weller 2014). In the CSU DAG for this fixture: T (remibrutinib) -> mast-cell quiescence -> UAS7 reduction (Y, primary) -> reduced itch/hives/sleep-disruption -> DLQI improvement. DLQI sits TWO STEPS DOWNSTREAM of treatment: it is a SECONDARY dermatology QoL DESCENDANT of the primary outcome Y rather than a parallel outcome on its own causal branch (Qian 2023 network meta-analysis explicitly documents the paired UAS7-then-DLQI response sequence in omalizumab CSU trials, with DLQI changes tracking UAS7 changes after a 1-2 week lag). Because DLQI is a descendant of Y, conditioning on it would induce selection bias on Y, absorb part of the treatment effect, and overadjust per VanderWeele 2015 mediation/overadjustment guidance. It is valid as a concordant secondary QoL endpoint for triangulation but MUST NOT be used as a regressor in the primary T->UAS7 estimation.

entries.rationale: Provider-volume is a Brookhart-family IV (catalogued in the Brookhart-Rassen-Schneeweiss 2010 IV review under prescriber/facility-level instruments) operationalized for refractory CSU. Z->T present: high-volume CSU prescribers preferentially initiate newer agents (BTKi vs continued omalizumab) due to formulary familiarity, pathway-tool exposure, and KOL practice patterns. NO Z->Y bypass: the original concern was that volume could directly affect UAS7 via three plausible direct paths -- (a) monitoring intensity, (b) referral-quality differentials, (c) escalation behavior. This entry CLOSES each path explicitly by analysis-stratum design: (a) monitoring intensity is held fixed by conditioning on patient-level visit-frequency strata AND on UCT-collection-completeness tertiles (UCT/UAS7 are patient-completed diaries per EAACI 2021, but completion rates correlate with practice infrastructure; stratification breaks the volume->completeness->measured-UAS7 path); (b) referral-quality is fixed by restricting the analytic cohort to refractory-CSU referral pool already-routed for biologic/BTKi consideration, removing the volume->triage->severity-at-index path; (c) escalation behavior (post-index dose changes, switch decisions) is post-baseline and NOT conditioned on, but the baseline volume tertile precedes them temporally and is unaffected. NO common cause: under case-mix balance audited per Brookhart 2007, volume operates on the prescriber side independent of individual patient prognosis. MANDATORY VALIDATION: report negative-control outcome (dental-visit rate, unrelated to CSU biology) by volume tertile per Brookhart 2007 IV-audit framework; failure of the negative-control check moves this entry to candidate-IV status.

NO Z->Y bypass requires three explicit design conditions, ALL mandatory for this entry to count as a gold instrument: (i) PAYER FIXED EFFECTS in the analytic model to absorb payer-level differences in supportive-care benefit design (H1AH coverage, dermatology copay structure, telehealth benefits) that could otherwise act on UAS7 directly; (ii) EXCLUDE quarters in which the tier change for remibrutinib was BUNDLED with other CSU-relevant formulary edits (omalizumab tier change, dupilumab addition, H1AH formulary restriction) -- bundled-quarter changes break the only-treatment-channel restriction and must be censored from the IV window; (iii) BLOCK DELAY-TO-CARE direct path by restricting to patients whose treatment initiation occurred within a fixed N-day window (e.g., 60 days) of the tier-change effective date -- longer delays admit a tier->delay->disease-progression->UAS7-baseline-shift pathway that violates exclusion. NO common cause: tier changes are driven by payer-pharmacy-economic considerations (rebate negotiations, generic-launch calendar) rather than patient prognosis at the individual level; payer-fixed-effects further absorb payer-pool case-mix differences.

The instrument operates at the prescriber-adoption-timing level and DOES NOT carry the direct Z->Y bypass paths that geographic or facility-level instruments would: (a) transfusion-management protocols are guideline-driven and uniform across early- vs late-adopter prescribers (Hill TRIUMPH 2010 protocol guidance), (b) breakthrough-hemolysis-management algorithms are publication-driven (Risitano 2019 SAAWP) and shared, (c) meningococcal-infection prophylaxis is REMS-mandated and uniform, (d) hemolysis-monitoring intensity follows IPNHR Schrezenmeier 2014 baseline-and-quarterly schedule used by both prescriber strata. Crucially the instrument is timing-conditional on a SHARED FDA approval event rather than on patient-side proximity to a specialty center, so it does not encode access-to-care or diagnosis-speed direct paths. No common cause: a prescriber's calendar-quarter-of-first-iptacopan is exogenous to any individual incident patient's complement biology. Brookhart 2010 catalogs combined calendar-discontinuity-plus-prescriber instruments as the strongest pharmacoepi IV family.
